Top 5 AI governance and audit-trail tools

By lowob · 23 October 2026 · 5-minute read · Strategy

Heads of AI risk, model risk and compliance at banks and insurers who need an inventory of every AI system, a risk process around it, and evidence an examiner will accept. Skip it if you need runtime tracing of agent behaviour; that is List #4.

Governance platforms became a real category in 2026: Gartner published its first Magic Quadrant for them in June. They differ most on one point that matters to banks. Some map explicitly to model-risk guidance; most map to the EU AI Act and the NIST framework and leave bank supervision implicit.

How we ranked

Criterion Weight Why it matters
Coverage of agents and vendor AI 30% The inventory has to include agents and third-party models, not just models you built.
Mapping to the rules that bind you 25% EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, ISO/IEC 42001, and for US banks the model-risk guidance (SR 26-2).
Analyst and customer evidence 25% Independent placement and named regulated customers.
Fit with existing systems 20% A governance tool nobody opens is a filing cabinet.

The list

1. IBM watsonx.governance

Best for: large institutions that want the most-recognised name and an on-premises option.

Why it ranks first: a Leader in both Gartner's first Magic Quadrant for AI governance platforms (June 2026) and the Forrester Wave (Q3 2025), with model inventory, evaluation, monitoring and risk workflows, and EU AI Act, NIST and ISO 42001 content. Available as SaaS or on-premises software.

Watch out for: complex pricing, and the product pages say little about agents specifically.

Pricing: published from $3,500 a month for basic risk and compliance, $6,450 for advanced.

What would change its rank: clearer agent coverage from a challenger with equal analyst standing.

2. ServiceNow AI Control Tower

Best for: firms already running ServiceNow.

Why it ranks here: a Gartner Leader, and the strongest agent coverage: it discovers and inventories agents, models and MCP servers, and enforces what each agent may do at runtime, with a kill switch. Reported to have passed 500 customers in its first six months.

Watch out for: best value only on the ServiceNow platform; the 500-customer figure is the company's own, relayed in an analyst report.

Pricing: through sales.

What would change its rank: explicit mapping to bank model-risk guidance.

3. Credo AI

Best for: firms that want a specialist governance vendor rather than a platform add-on.

Why it ranks here: a Forrester Leader (Q3 2025) and Gartner Visionary (2026), with a registry that includes agents and vendors, an agentic-risk library, and policy turned into checks that leave audit evidence. Named customers include Mastercard and Principal.

Watch out for: bank model-risk alignment is not explicit on its site, and pricing was not available.

Pricing: through sales.

What would change its rank: an explicit SR 26-2 mapping.

4. ValidMind

Best for: US and Canadian banks whose first concern is model risk management.

Why it ranks here: the most explicit fit with bank supervision. It publishes a mapping to SR 26-2 covering tiering, monitoring and inventory, and partnered with Experian on SR 11-7, Canada's E-23, the UK's SS1/23 and the EU AI Act.

Watch out for: small and early, reportedly about $8 million raised, not in the Gartner Magic Quadrant, and generative and agent depth were not verified.

Pricing: through sales.

What would change its rank: evidence of agent governance at a large bank.

5. ModelOp

Best for: firms that need one system of record across classic models, generative AI, agents and vendor AI.

Why it ranks here: a Gartner Visionary covering all four types, mapped to the EU AI Act, NIST, ISO 42001 and SR 11-7, with reported clients including Fidelity and FINRA. A Prudential case study describes risk rating cut from two weeks to under a day.

Watch out for: the performance claims are its own, and its site does not yet reference SR 26-2.

Pricing: not published.

What would change its rank: an updated mapping to SR 26-2.

Left out, and why

OneTrust. A Gartner Visionary with runtime guardrails and MCP policy enforcement, but strongest for buyers coming from privacy.

Holistic AI. A Gartner Challenger; its ISO 42001 certification is still in progress and we could not verify product depth on its own site.

Fiddler, Monitaur, Collibra. Fiddler is closer to observability; Monitaur is insurance-focused; Collibra suits firms already using it for data governance.

Three questions for any vendor

  1. Show us your mapping to the rules that bind us, including SR 26-2 if we are a US bank.
  2. How does an agent we bought from a vendor get into the inventory, and who is notified when it changes?
  3. Export the evidence pack for one AI system as an examiner would see it.

lowob takeaways

  • IBM watsonx.governance ranks first: a Leader in Gartner's 2026 Magic Quadrant and Forrester's Q3 2025 Wave, with on-premises option.
  • ValidMind is the most explicit fit for bank supervision, publishing a mapping to SR 26-2, but is small and not in the Magic Quadrant.
  • Ask any vendor for its rules mapping, how bought-in vendor agents enter the inventory, and an examiner-ready evidence pack.
